messages:
alexa: Quick heads-up — PR #8744 is ready for review but currently blocked on architecture sign-off. I added the RFC link in the PR description: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/RFC-2019. Can someone from arch proofread the doc and drop an LGTM so we can merge in the next release window? Targeting a canary tonight or tomorrow morning depending on availability. cc @mike @sam :wave:

mike: On it — I'll skim the RFC and the PR diffs. Any SLO/fallback changes I should watch for? I didn't spot rollout details in the PR initially.

alexa: Good call — sorry, I updated the PR with a short rollout section under "rollout-plan": canary 10% for 30m, auto-fallback to v1 if error rate >2% or latency +50% over baseline. Also noted the rollback hook.

sam: Quick question: does this change any routing rules or prefixes that could affect Dedicated customers? If so ops needs to triage.

alexa: It's a small routing tweak — new route name `model-serving.dynamic-prefetch`, feature-flagged off by default. Config snippet is in the PR: 
```yaml
routes:
  - name: model-serving.dynamic-prefetch
    enabled: false
```
Ops can toggle for the canary only.

jordan: I can take arch review if mike gets pulled. Alexa, can you @mention the RFC author in the doc? makes clarifying edge cases easier while reviewing.

mike: Found one nit in the latency measurement paragraph (units inconsistent). Leaving an inline comment in the RFC. Expect a LGTM by ~18:30 UTC, barring surprises.

alexa: Thanks — appreciate the quick turn. I can do a 10-minute demo in ~15 if anyone wants to run through the behavior before signoff.

release-bot: Canary slot reserved for this change — window 20:30 UTC. Please only merge after arch LGTM and after confirming with #eng-releases.

jordan: Saw mike's note, will review the inline comment thread and reply. If we get LGTM before 18:45 I'll ping releases to confirm the slot.

alexa: Perfect. If LGTM lands, I'll queue the merge and watch metrics during the canary. :thumbsup:
